title: Service Interruption: Customer Recovery & Remediation Obligations (Template)
content:
Purpose:
This template module is intended to be included as a stand-alone exhibit or as part of a broader Services Agreement when Redwood Inference ("Provider") and a Customer agree on obligations that govern: (1) what Provider will do after a class of service interruptions; (2) how Customer data and derived artifacts will be preserved and returned; and (3) the limited remedies and operational support the Provider will provide to facilitate customer recovery.

Scope and Applicability:
- Applies only to outages, degraded service incidents, and feature regression events that materially prevent Customer from using the Service for production traffic.
- Not intended to apply to: scheduled maintenance when notice is provided per the Agreement; issues caused by Customer misconfiguration; or third-party outages outside Provider control (except as explicitly stated below).

Key Definitions (negotiation notes in brackets):
- "Service Interruption": a continuous period longer than [X] minutes during which successful requests for production inference return errors or timeouts at a rate greater than [Y]%.
- "Material Degradation": sustained increase in 95th percentile latency above agreed SLO by >[Z]% for [A] consecutive minutes.
- "Customer Recovery Package (CRP)": the set of deliverables Provider must make available to Customer to enable recovery and verification of Customer functionality.

Customer Recovery Obligations (Provider Deliverables):
1) Immediate Operational Actions (within initial Triage Window):
   - Acknowledge and classify incident severity within [30] minutes of detection or Customer report.
   - Open a dedicated incident channel (pager/slack) and assign an incident commander.
   - Provide rolling incident status updates at least every [60] minutes until mitigated.

2) Short-term Remediation (24–72 hours):
   - Restore production traffic to baseline throughput or provide an accepted fall-back model variant that meets an agreed performance profile.
   - If service cannot be restored to baseline, provide a temporary routing or export path for Customer to re-run pending requests (see Export & Replay below).

3) Customer Recovery Package (CRP) contents (delivered no later than 7 business days after incident resolution unless otherwise agreed):
   - Incident report describing root cause, sequence of events, and corrective actions.
   - Time-bounded export of Customer-submitted inference inputs, outputs generated during the incident window, and associated metadata (timestamps, request-ids, model-version ids). Export format: ndjson (or agreed equivalent).
   - A sanitized snapshot of relevant KV/prefix caches, key manifests, and model variant mappings sufficient to replay or rehydrate Customer state in a compatible environment.
   - If requested, an architectural runbook outlining steps Customer must perform to re-play requests in their environment or in a Provider-test sandbox.

Export & Replay Procedure (evidence and controls):
- Exports will exclude system logs, internal worker debug traces, and any third-party customer identifiers unless expressly authorized.
- Customer may request cryptographic proof of export integrity (SHA256 checksums) and a signed manifest listing exported files.
- Provider will hold exported data for [30] days from delivery to Customer for recovery assistance; thereafter, stored exports will be deleted unless Customer instructs otherwise in writing.

Data Preservation & Chain-of-Custody:
- During the mitigation and CRP delivery windows, Provider will preserve original artifacts and metadata associated with the incident in a dedicated, access-controlled repository.
- Access to preserved artifacts by Provider personnel is logged; Customer audit requests and limited read-access for recovery assistance to a named Customer representative can be provided on request.

Escalation & Communication:
- Escalation path: Incident Commander -> Ops Lead -> VP Eng -> Customer Success -> Legal (if requested).
- Provider will make available a post-incident review call within [10] business days of incident closure.
- Public communications requiring Customer-specific impact statements will not be issued without Customer approval.

Service Credits, Limitations, and Remedies:
- If Provider fails to meet the obligations in this exhibit, Customer may be eligible for Service Credits defined as: [for each full 24-hour period of unmitigated outage beyond initial response], a credit equal to [X%] of the monthly fees attributable to the affected service for each day, capped at [Y%] of monthly fees.
- Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive monetary remedy for outages; Customer may still seek injunctive relief where lawful.
- Provider shall not be liable for indirect or consequential damages arising from interruption, except where prohibited by applicable law.

Testing, Audit, and Operational Readiness:
- Provider commits to a quarterly tabletop exercise with Customer (or with a shared channel) to validate export, replay, and CRP delivery processes.
- Provider will maintain documented runbooks; Customer may request evidence of runbook tests and a summary of last three incidents and lessons learned (redacted for other customers).

Optional Add-ons / Enterprise Options (checkbox items for negotiation):
- Dedicated backup exports: continuous archival of production inference inputs/outputs to Customer-managed storage for an additional fee.
- On-call liaison: assignment of a named engineer for periodic drills and for live incidents during Customer business hours.
- Extended export retention: Provider to retain exports for [90/180/365] days per Customer choice.

Operational Implementation Notes (internal guidance):
- Notes to Legal: prefer 30–90 day export retention as default; require Customer to accept responsibility for storage costs if retention extends beyond 30 days.
- Notes to Ops/Product: ensure endpoint-level request-id tagging and consistent model-version identifiers to make CRP exports actionable.
- Notes to Sales/CS: put optional add-ons in clause library with pricing bands for negotiations.

Negotiation Redlines / Risk Flags for Legal Counsel:
- Avoid open-ended retention commitments.
- Limit export scope to Customer-submitted data + Provider-generated outputs; exclude unredacted system traces that could disclose other customers' telemetry.
- Where Customer requires regulatory evidence (e.g., for SOC2/PCI), include a separate exhibit describing limited audit access and required NDAs.

Checklist for Inclusion in Master Agreement (to attach to SOW or SLA):
- [ ] Define thresholds (X, Y, Z) for interruption and degradation.
- [ ] Agree CRP delivery timeline and export format.
- [ ] Select any optional add-ons and retention period.
- [ ] Include contact and escalation list with 24/7 vs business-hours designations.

Open Questions (internal):
- Should we offer replay-as-a-service for a fixed fee (Provider replays requests back through restored model on Customer's behalf)? Pros/cons for liability and cost.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, how to handle cross-account KV cache snapshot transfer without shared storage?

Appendix A: Example CRP Delivery Manifest (sample fields) - (deliver as separate file with export):
- manifest.json: {"customer_id": "<id>", "incident_window": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ to YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ", "files": ["inputs.ndjson", "outputs.ndjson", "cache_manifest.json"]}

(Implementation note: manifest.json above is illustrative; CRP exports should be supplied with checksums and a signed cover note.)

Document History / Versioning:
- Draft 0.1 (2024-09-12) initial template by Evelyn Park.
- Draft 0.2 (2024-10-03) Ops comments incorporated (Mateo).
- Draft 0.3 (2024-11-06) Legal redlines and optional add-ons enumerated.

End of template.

Internal remarks: This is meant to be modular; copy as Exhibit X and reference the Service Level and Incident Response sections in the master contract. Keep negotiation-friendly placeholders and prefer limiting retention/transfer obligations unless compensated.
